role: LLM-driven knowledge graph connection formation during consolidation idle periods
detail: Synaptogenesis periodically examines new knowledge graph nodes (capped 50/cycle), expands 2-hop neighborhood for context, calls Claude with a structured prompt to propose new edges and ConceptPrimitive nodes, validates all proposals against graph state, and commits at low confidence (edges: 0.15, concepts/procedures: 0.20). Supports three proposal types: edges between existing nodes, abstract category ConceptPrimitives with IS_A members, and composite ActionProcedure nodes with HAS_SUB_PROCEDURE and RELIEVES edges. Uses a meta-schema node (meta:synaptogenesis_state) to persist last-run watermark timestamp, enabling differential queries on subsequent cycles. All proposals carry INFERENCE provenance with source_id="synaptogenesis". Fire-and-forget pattern: LLM failures log and return empty report without blocking consolidation.
gotchas: Frontier node logic in _expand_neighborhood (line 584-586) has redundant assignment that may be a bug—frontier is set twice, second time overwriting the intended deduplication. LLM call is fire-and-forget with no retry; prompt strips markdown fencing preemptively. Procedure proposals require preconditions to be non-empty dict; all referenced sub-procedure IDs must be in known_node_ids (2-hop neighborhood only). Edge deduplication checks both specific edge_id and EdgeFilter query for same type/source/target—belt-and-suspenders approach.
